brief: The Fed delivered its first hike last week; FOMC details were hawkish, penciling in one additional hike alongside stronger growth, lower unemployment, and stickier inflation. Inflation has stalled above target and worsened over the past year; Chair Warsh signaled impatience for price stability "on a timelier basis," framing the choice as hiking now versus hiking more later. PNC expects two more hikes (December, next March), three total, but says risks skew toward more, not fewer, since the September SEP shows core PCE returning to target only in 2029 and interim-year projections were revised higher. Because oil prices and AI capex are largely rate-insensitive, PNC sees a plausible path where the Fed keeps hiking until tighter financial conditions weaken the stock market enough to cool wealth-effect-driven spending, as happened in the 2022-23 cycle. PNC views today's hiking risk as higher than 2022-23: with only one job vacancy per unemployed worker versus two in 2022, further hikes risk a proportionately larger rise in unemployment, and excess savings have already fallen from their post-pandemic highs.
